text:
The Capitals have now won three straight, and the one that kept it going on Nashville ice leaned on a 20-year-old defenseman. Cole Hutson scored twice for WSH, the first on a 2% chance late in the opening period, and the second a snap shot in the middle frame that put WSH ahead 3-2. Hutson was drafted 43rd overall in 2024 out of the U.S. national under-18 program, and he came to the NHL after a 48-point season at Boston University. Alex Tuch added the winner at 10:09 of the third, a wrist shot on a 6% chance, 3 minutes and 35 seconds after Ross Colton had tied it at 3-3.

By our numbers, Nashville was the better team. We rate the quality of each shot as expected goals, and NSH finished with 2.98 to WSH's 2.77. Run the night's chances through simulated replays and NSH comes out ahead 54% of the time. WSH took the second period, 1.51 to 0.64 in expected goals, but NSH controlled the first and third, and 34 of the 56 faceoffs. Filip Forsberg scored twice, once on the power play, and missed the net on a 21% look in the third that would have been the go-ahead goal. Roman Josi had three assists and 6 shots on goal, and NSH created 2.41 expected goals with him on the ice against 0.81 allowed.

For NSH, that's a 4-3 loss in a game its play suggested it should have won, and Juuse Saros allowed 1.2 goals more than his 29 shots deserved. The Capitals stretch their streak to three and head home with the points.
